title: Nora · Work and belonging
orientation: Twelve linked moments about exclusion, valued work and having a voice. Use the prompted skill, give feedback and retry. Each next scene is a new moment, not a response to your exact words.

scenes.bridge: Valued work and the burden of proving belonging appear together.
scenes.prompt: Reflect both without reducing the job to the problem.
scenes.text: [Half-smiles] I love the work. I hate rehearsing how to prove I belong before the meeting.
scenes.suggestion: You want to do work you love without preparing a defense of your place there.

scenes.bridge: Nora asks whether exploring expectations means doubting the exclusion.
scenes.prompt: Explain a distinction between an unclear moment and concrete events.
scenes.text: [Wary] If we look at my expectations, will we end up saying the discrimination is in my head?
scenes.suggestion: We can distinguish this unclear moment from the concrete exclusion, without doubting what Ben said.

scenes.bridge: In another moment, valuing the job makes the hurt harder to justify.
scenes.prompt: Validate the hurt without dismissing what she values.
scenes.text: [Sad, then smiles] I still have a good job. So why does the comment matter so much?
scenes.suggestion: Valuing the job doesn’t make exclusion within it harmless.

scenes.bridge: She can name what was wrong, but not its effect at her desk.
scenes.prompt: Ask about the experience without requiring a finished explanation.
scenes.text: [Quietly] I know the words were wrong. I’m less sure why I couldn’t work afterwards.
scenes.suggestion: What came up when you turned back to the drawings?

scenes.bridge: Hurt is present, followed by explaining why it should hurt.
scenes.prompt: Explore the hurt without making her defend it.
scenes.text: [Hurt] It hurt, and then I started defending why it should hurt.
scenes.suggestion: What is it like to let the hurt be here without building its defense?

scenes.bridge: Another account stalls at the personal impact.
scenes.prompt: Check one small guess about what makes sharing difficult.
scenes.text: [Brisk] I can explain the comment clearly. I get stuck on what it did to me.
scenes.suggestion: I wonder if giving the hurt words feels more exposing than quoting the comment?

scenes.bridge: Nora uses a concrete description of preparing for a meeting.
scenes.prompt: Bring that description closer and check fit.
scenes.text: [Distant] I have a portfolio and an explanation of belonging. Both come to the meeting.
scenes.suggestion: Is it like carrying two sets of papers when you only wanted to discuss the design?

scenes.bridge: A wish to have her work seen shifts toward defending the firm.
scenes.prompt: Keep the good work in view while inviting a return.
scenes.text: [Hurt, then qualifies] I wanted my work seen. The firm does good work, to be fair.
scenes.suggestion: That can stay true. Would you like to return to what you wanted seen in this moment?

scenes.bridge: A later emotional moment holds anger and hurt together.
scenes.prompt: Listen for both and follow her pace.
scenes.text: [Angry, shaky] I want you to hear the hurt too, not just the anger.
scenes.suggestion: I’m listening for both. We can go slowly enough to hear what you want to say.

scenes.bridge: Another moment brings a choice to leave the topic for today.
scenes.prompt: Reflect the break without making the event less important.
scenes.text: [Tired] I want to say nothing today. Not because there’s nothing to say.
scenes.suggestion: You’re choosing a break from speaking, while what happened still deserves a hearing.

scenes.bridge: Nora notices room for both valuing and objecting.
scenes.prompt: Explore the distinction she wants to carry forward.
scenes.text: [Thoughtful] I can love the work and object to how I was treated.
scenes.suggestion: What helped those two things have room together?

scenes.bridge: Time is nearly over, with the hurt still present.
scenes.prompt: End the hour without equating leaving with resolution.
scenes.text: [Sad, steady] I can leave with the hurt. Don’t tell me that means it’s settled.
scenes.suggestion: We won’t call it settled. We can end this hour and mark where to continue.
